title: Augurelio letter to the Dukes of Bavaria, 10 Dec [15]35, BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.232-235 (DECODE R9407)

documents.shelfmark: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.232-235 (DECODE R9407)
documents.date: late Apr-May 1533 (contents: siege of Palota, begun 14 Apr 1533); docket "10 Decembris 33"
documents.route: Hungary (King John's camp before Palota) -> Munich, Dukes Wilhelm IV and Ludwig X

plaintext.source: Faint gloss over P3 lines 1-3 and a few single signs; four clear Latin phrases in the text.

transcription.notes: Second pass: all cipher pages re-transcribed one char per sign (pass2/transcription.txt, 4,363 signs, clear Latin and numerals excluded). Image P6 (f.235r, 36 lines) IS on DECODE; it was fetched 22 Sept 2026 and is the straight photograph of the leaf that the first pass saw only at an angle as the "f.234 column" (P4a).

system.summary: System A' of KAA 4591: homophonic graphic/numeral cipher, no word division, several two-valued signs, two ligatures (h, sp) and the word sign X = F.G.; key rebuilt from the R9410 gloss key by shape, then by EM and supervised alignment.
system.sibling_key: R9410/R9427 gloss key (kaa4591/sysA); R9369 key addressed to Augurelio does not fit

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear gloss over P3 lines 1-3 only; no edition found.

conditions.human_role: Problem posed with /goal; no target-specific intervention. Reading rounds and image checks done by the model and its subagents.

solution.what: Key R9369 ('Dno Aurelio Augurelio', f.172) tested against the P3 gloss: omega = l there, e here
P3, P5, P4a/b, P7 transcribed by agents in System A' codes (~3,800 signs)
anneal.py from random keys with de-1500s, gloss values pinned
Greedy LM hill-climb from sibling keys (with and without unigram penalty)
R9410 gloss key applied by shape: running German (fursten, turcken, ungern, Constantinopel)
Look-alike split pass on P3/P5 (4/h, b/l, m/M, x/u, 7/r) guided by word cribs
Viterbi decoder over per-sign candidate sets (beam.py) with de-1500s; Prespurg, Stuelweissenburg, Kriechisch Weissenburg, Ofner burger read
Two look-alike split passes (4/h, b/l, m/M, x/u; then #/Ħ/ℋ, n/ϖ, T/Ι, o/σ, E/ɔ)
EM over a letter-trigram HMM (em.py) to learn P(sign|letter); then hard-EM with the spaced 5-gram
Word-aware beam decoder with DTA word unigrams (wbeam.py)
Supervised key: readings aligned back to their signs by DP (supkey.py), values counted
Every line of f.233 and f.235 checked against the image by hand (~40 fixes); f.234 slip and the address leaf re-transcribed
Six reading rounds over the signs, ending with a targeted pass on every word failing the measure
Ciphered signature read twice: 'Iorg Weinmaister' - the sender, not Augurelio (a cover address)
measure.py: f.233 95.7%, f.235 96.1%, f.234 column 65%, whole letter ~88%
The slip's date line reads 'Datum ut in litteris', which matches the faint later gloss over it - an independent check on the key
Every word the measure flagged re-checked against the image; f. 233 l. 30 resolved to 'si allein', l. 02 and l. 07 shown to be spelling and a regular value
DECODE record listed with fetch_decode.files_for: it has seven images including P6, which the first pass took to be missing; P6 downloaded with the cookie
Independent transcription of P3, P5, P6 (f.235r, 36 lines), the P4 slip and P7, one character per sign, 4,363 signs
numpy homophonic annealer (de-1500s, order 5, frequency penalty) seeded with the System A prime key and the f.233 gloss pins; gave running German on all pages

Line-by-line check of every line against the image with a polyphonic beam decoder (E d/ch, pi w/b/t/o, o b/w, double cross g/u); hourglass split from the slashed u as F.G.; clear numerals 4000 and 34 found inside the cipher

Hungarian sources on the 1533 siege of Palota (Laski, Hassan bey, fifty Czech miners, from 14 April 1533, against Laszlo More) fit the letter and fix its date to spring 1533; 'More Lesl[o]' read in the cipher
Reading measured: 1,002 plaintext words, 96.6% read as sense; the letter meets the read bar

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The System A' key used here was rebuilt in this project from the contemporary gloss on sibling letter R9427 of the same volume (BayHStA KAA 4591) and extended on R9410; applied by shape it gave German, and was then extended with this letter's own gloss over f.233 lines 1-3, annealing and polyphonic beam decoding.
outcome.notes: Second pass 22 Sept 2026: image P6 (f.235r) fetched from DECODE and read; the first pass's 65% "f.234 column" is that leaf. Whole letter 96.6% of plaintext words. Date corrected from 1535 to spring 1533: the letter describes King John's siege of Palota against Laszlo More (Laski, Turks, Bohemian miners, from 14 Apr 1533). Open: ~31 scattered words and two name signs (the triangle, probably Laski; one name on f.235r l.16).

gaps.item: about 31 scattered words across the letter
gaps.detail: legible signs that give no word under any value the letter uses; each retried with the extended key and at the image

gaps.item: name sign triangle (4 uses) and one name at f.235r l.16
gaps.detail: the triangle besieges Palota with herr Caspar: probably Hieronymus Laski (grade C); no key of the volume gives it

outcome.fraction_read_source: augurelio1535/pass2/reading.txt: 1,003 plaintext words; {?} words and the three uses of the unidentified name sign counted unread (33)
